teaser: The reception hall empties out around midnight, folding chairs stacked, the last cousins hugging goodbye at the door, and you are the one still circling with a trash bag nobody handed you. You carry 33, the master number your birth date adds to before it reduces to a single digit, and the letters ESFJ, and this crossing makes the circling look natural, even necessary, rather than something chosen. What's particular here is how little this crossing distinguishes between the people you love and the people at the next table: both get the same attention, the same instinct to smooth the evening so no one goes home unhappy.
excerpt: A thermos passed hand to hand around a campsite at night, refilled before anyone asks, is the shape love takes here.
